checklistGeneric: Each tolerance traced to an approved risk appetite limit
Deviations documented and approved
checklistSpecific: Express each tolerance as a maximum tolerable outage duration plus a volume or value of affected customers
Cross-check every tolerance against the supervisor's stated resilience expectation for that service
Test each tolerance against the customer-harm scenario (payment missed, claim unpaid, cover unavailable) and tighten it where harm arises earlier
Confirm no tolerance is looser than the existing BCP recovery time objective for the same service
Record the alignment decision per service in the resilience register

testing.expected: No important business service with a tolerance exceeding its BCP recovery time objective

checklistGeneric: Distribution list covers every accountable owner
Receipt acknowledged and recorded
checklistSpecific: Issue each business unit head only the tolerance set for the services they own, not the full register
Send technology and third-party managers the tolerance-derived recovery targets for the systems that support each service
Confirm each recipient acknowledges the tolerance as a binding target and names their delivery owner
Publish the tolerance summary on the resilience site showing the version and approval date

testing.expected: No service owner without a recorded acknowledgement

checklistGeneric: Each entry has a named accountable owner
Definitions reviewed by a second party
checklistSpecific: Write each definition as a customer outcome (for example, a claim is paid) rather than an internal function
Record for each service the customers served, the channels used, typical volumes, and the regulatory driver
Confirm each documented service maps to at least one regulatory expectation and one customer-harm scenario
Reconcile the documented list against the candidate inventory and record why any candidate was excluded

testing.expected: No registered service without an accountable owner and a customer-outcome definition

checklistGeneric: Rationale recorded against the version of the tolerance it supports
Evidence sources cited
checklistSpecific: Record for each tolerance the data used to set the timeframe (complaint volumes, payment cycles, claim settlement SLAs)
State the point at which customer harm becomes intolerable and show how the timeframe was derived from it
Document the severity dimension (proportion of customers, value at risk) and its basis
Note the assumptions, data limitations, and the review trigger that would invalidate the rationale

testing.expected: No tolerance record with an empty rationale or a missing evidence source

checklistGeneric: Papers issued in advance of the meeting
Challenge and responses recorded
checklistSpecific: Circulate the draft services list with the inclusion criteria and the excluded candidates ahead of the executive session
Walk the committee through the most contested services and the basis for their classification
Capture each challenge raised and either the agreed change or the reason no change was made
Confirm the executive and board position on the final list before requesting formal approval

testing.location: Executive engagement pack and meeting notes
testing.expected: Notes recording challenge, responses, and the confirmed list version

checklistGeneric: Approval recorded in the minutes with the version approved
Approver holds documented authority
checklistSpecific: Submit the final services list and tolerance set as a Board paper with the rationale appendix attached
Confirm the minute records approval of the list and of each impact tolerance, not of the paper generally
Record the approved version number and effective date in the resilience register
Log any Board condition or requested follow-up as a tracked action with an owner and due date

testing.location: Important business service register, approval fields
testing.expected: Board approval date, minute reference, and approved version recorded

checklistGeneric: Review date and reviewer recorded on every entry
Changes version-controlled with an audit trail
checklistSpecific: Run the annual review and confirm each service definition, owner, and tolerance is still valid
Assess material changes since the last review (new products, new outsourcing, system replacement, acquisitions) for new candidate services
Retire services no longer offered and record the retirement rationale and date
Re-baseline tolerances where volumes, channels, or customer profiles have shifted materially
Set the next review date and record the trigger events that force an off-cycle refresh

testing.location: Important business service register, review date field
testing.expected: No register entry with a review date older than twelve months

checklistGeneric: Submission reviewed for accuracy before filing
Submission receipt retained
checklistSpecific: Prepare the resilience return in the supervisor's prescribed format covering services, tolerances, and approval dates
Reconcile every figure in the return to the approved register version rather than to working drafts
Obtain second-line compliance review and sign-off before submission
Submit by the supervisory deadline and retain the submission receipt and reference number
Log the submission in the regulatory filing inventory with its next due date

testing.location: Regulatory filing inventory, resilience return entry
testing.expected: Submission logged with receipt reference and next due date

checklistGeneric: Approver authority verified against the delegation matrix
Signed record retained
checklistSpecific: Route the final definition set to the accountable executive for each service for individual sign-off
Confirm each executive signs the specific service definition and owner assignment, not a summary list
Record the sign-off name, role, date, and document version against each definition
Chase and escalate any definition still unsigned five working days before publication

testing.expected: No service definition without a dated executive signature

checklistGeneric: Only the approved version is published
Superseded versions archived rather than deleted
checklistSpecific: Publish the approved definitions to the resilience site with the version and approval date visible
Archive the previous version and mark it superseded so it cannot be mistaken for current
Notify service owners, business continuity, and technology leads that the new baseline is live
Confirm the published set matches the Board-approved register entry by entry

testing.expected: Current approved version published with approval date and prior versions archived

checklistGeneric: Threshold expressed in measurable, testable terms
Accountable owner named for each threshold
checklistSpecific: Set a maximum tolerable disruption duration for each important business service in hours or days
Define the severity measure (customers affected, transactions failed, value delayed) with a numeric limit
Confirm the threshold can be measured from existing operational data before agreeing it
Define the breach escalation trigger, who must be notified, and within what timeframe
Enter each threshold against its service in the resilience register with the effective date

testing.expected: No important business service without a numeric duration and severity threshold

checklistGeneric: The same criteria applied to every candidate
Classification decision and reviewer recorded
checklistSpecific: Score each candidate service against the customer-harm criteria (financial loss, loss of cover, vulnerable-customer impact)
Score each candidate against the market-impact criteria (volume, market share, concentration, substitutability)
Apply the agreed threshold to mark each candidate important or not important, leaving no candidate unscored
Record the reason for every not-important outcome so exclusions can be challenged
Have a second reviewer confirm the borderline classifications before the list is finalised

testing.expected: No candidate service left unclassified or classified without a recorded reason

checklistGeneric: Inventory sourced from an authoritative catalogue
Completeness confirmed with each business owner
checklistSpecific: Extract the candidate list from the product catalogue and the process model covering every live line of business
Add the customer journeys (new business, renewal, claims, complaints, payments) as candidate services
Confirm with each business owner that no customer-facing service they run is missing from the list
Drop internal functions that are not customer-facing outcomes and record why each was dropped
Record for each candidate the owner, line of business, and customer channel

testing.expected: No live line of business absent from the candidate inventory

checklistGeneric: Mapping validated with each resource owner
Map version-controlled and dated
checklistSpecific: Map for each important business service the people, processes, technology, facilities, data, and third parties it depends on
Trace the applications end to end from customer entry point to settlement, including interfaces and batch jobs
Identify the third parties and intra-group providers in the chain and record their contract and exit arrangements
Flag single points of failure and resources shared across more than one important business service
Reconcile the mapped applications to CMDB records and raise a gap where a dependency is not registered

testing.location: Service dependency mapping for important business services
testing.expected: No mapped application dependency missing a CMDB configuration item
